data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Habibur can be related to various Hindu deities and divine figures. For instance, in the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna, who is considered as the supreme beloved, refers to Arjuna as "Mama Bhootam Dhara" (My dear Arjuna). This can be translated to mean "dear one to me." Similarly, Shiva, a popular Hindu god, is often depicted as the destroyer-cum-protector, and his devotees address him as "Hara Bhajan," meaning "beloved Hara," indicating a deep spiritual bond. In this way, the name Habibur, resonating with the essence of love, affection, and devotion, could be a reminder of the profound connection established between a soul and a deity.

historical_references.reference: Bengal Sultanate (1204-1538 AD) - The Sultans of Bengal adopted local names during their rule. Habibur Rahman Shah (1422-1442 AD) was the Sultan of Bengal and the founder of the Hussain Shahi Dynasty. He was the son of Sultan Shamsuddin I (Shahzada Jalaluddin Muhammad), who ruled from 1390 to 1414 AD.
historical_references.context: Founder of the Hussain Shahi Dynasty in Bengal Sultanate

historical_references.reference: Mughal Empire (1526-1858 AD) - Habibur Rahman Khan was a famous general and a nobleman in the Mughal Empire. He served under the Mughal Emperor Jahangir (1562-1627 AD). He was the father of the famous painter, Manohar, who was the court painter of Emperor Shah Jahan (1592-1666 AD).
